name: search_securities
description: Find securities by ticker or name. Returns every match across time, including delisted and renamed securities, each with security_id, name, asset_class, status and full ticker_history. Use this when a name is given instead of a ticker, or when resolve returns nothing. An empty query lists every security the app holds.

query.description: A ticker or part of a name.

name: resolve
description: Which security a ticker referred to on a given date. Returns one security record, or null if the ticker meant nothing on that date. Call it for every symbol in the form, once with the form's start date and once with its end date. If the two answers differ, the ticker was renamed or reused inside the range: tell the user and do not pick one silently.

name: get_coverage
description: The data held for a security: the primary series' first_bar, last_bar, gaps, adjustments, quality_tier and license, plus every synthetic recipe targeting it with its validation numbers. This is the only source for inception dates, coverage, expense ratios and leverage factors.

name: list_regimes
description: Named stress periods (dot-com bust, 2008 financial crisis, ...) that overlap a date range, with their exact dates.

name: save_form
description: Save the current Strategy Form. The app keeps it for the run; the user does not see it unless they open it. Call it as soon as you have a draft and again after every change, so the saved form always matches the conversation. With ready=false the form may contain nulls for fields whose provenance source is 'missing'. With ready=true it is validated strictly against the schema: on success the user sees a Run button, on failure you get the validation errors back and must fix them before saying anything to the user.

form.description: A Strategy Form, as defined by strategy_form.schema.json.

name: ask_user
description: Ask the user to choose values for form fields. Shown in the chat as buttons, with a box for a free-text answer, under `message`. Ask at most three questions per call. Each question is tied to the field it fills. Your turn ends when you ask: the user's answers come back as this tool's result.

message.description: What the user should know before answering, shown above the questions: what you found in the data (a shortened range, a symbol not held) and anything else that bears on the choices. Plain English, a few sentences at most. Text you write before calling a tool does not reach the user; this does.

path.description: JSON Pointer of the form field this answers, e.g. /strategy/exit/rules.

question.description: One short question in plain English.

label.description: Plain English, e.g. 'Sell when it gets back to the old high'.

value.description: The exact value written into the form at path if chosen.

hint.description: Optional one-line consequence, e.g. 'Fewer trades, longer time in cash'.

name: start_run
description: Run the saved form, which must have been accepted by save_form with ready=true and not changed since. Call it only when the user has asked for the run. The run takes from seconds to a few minutes; its results come back to you in a later message beginning with <results>, or <refused> if the job could not honour the form.
